fields.description:
Mirror inventory finding F3 (`reports/stability/mirror-inventory.md`), HIGH, comments already drifted.

## Problem

Which ticket types the plan-review gate reviews is one fact with SIX masters, and nothing
asserts they partition `TicketType`:

**Exempt** — `("bug", "session_log", "code_review", "identity")`
- `_commands/gates.py:45` `_PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES` (start-work gate)
- `_commands/composer.py:47` `_FILE_IMPACT_EXEMPT_TYPES` (create-time file-impact nudge)
- `llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:560` — inline literal

**Complement** — `("task", "story", "epic")`
- `llm/plan_review/claimability.py:38` `_REVIEWED_TYPES`
- `_commands/transition_close.py:46` `_PLAN_REVIEW_CLOSE_TYPES`
- `_commands/gates.py:215` — inline literal

`TicketType` (`types.py:23`) has exactly seven members, so 4 + 3 partitions it TODAY. The defect
is that nothing holds it that way: an eighth type lands in NEITHER set and is then neither gated
nor exempted. This decides whether the plan-review claim gate runs at all.

The single-sourcing claims are false, and one is drifted beyond being merely optimistic:
- `gates.py:42-44` — "Single-sourced here so ... cannot drift". It is not; five other sites exist.
- `composer.py:42-46` — admits "Kept in lockstep with", and MISDESCRIBES its counterpart: it cites
  the orchestrator as a "bug/session_log short-circuit before P9", but `orchestrator.py:560` sits
  inside the attestation DRIFT-REFRESH candidate path, not P9. Verified by reading the enclosing
  docstring.
- `claimability.py:40-41` prose names 2 of the 4 exempt types.

The only test is `assert "bug" in ...` (`test_bug_blast_radius_escalation_ad0d.py:199`).

## Approach — single-source the pair, then assert the partition

`types.py` already owns `TicketType` and is a true leaf (its only import is `typing`), so it is
the canonical home. Declare the exemption there and DERIVE its complement, so the two can never
disagree:

    PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES = frozenset({"bug", "session_log", "code_review", "identity"})
    PLAN_REVIEW_REVIEWED_TYPES = frozenset(get_args(TicketType)) - PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES

Then point all six sites at them.

**On epic AC2 (do not collapse a distinct concept).** The six sites serve four consumers — the
start-work gate, the create-time file-impact nudge, drift-refresh applicability, and the close
gate. They are not four different rules; they are four consumers of ONE predicate: "is this a
type whose plan the plan-review gate reviews?" Drift-refresh refreshes a plan-review
ATTESTATION, which only exists for reviewed types, so it is the same question. `composer`'s own
comment states the lockstep intent explicitly, so referencing one constant is faithful to the
author's intent rather than a merge of unrelated sets. If a consumer ever needs to diverge, that
becomes an explicit reviewed change instead of silent drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: `types.py` declares the exemption and derives the complement, and a test asserts the
      two are disjoint and their union is exactly `set(get_args(TicketType))`. Verified by that
      test failing if a member is added to `TicketType` without being placed in either set.
- [ ] AC2: all six sites reference the canonical constants; no ticket-type literal tuple remains
      at any of them. Verified by a test that greps the six modules for a re-listed exempt or
      reviewed tuple and finds none.
- [ ] AC3: adding a hypothetical eighth `TicketType` member fails the partition test rather than
      silently defaulting. Verified by the test parameterizing over an extended member set.
- [ ] AC4: the three false/drifted comments are corrected — `gates.py`'s "cannot drift" claim,
      `composer.py`'s misdescription of `orchestrator.py:560` as a P9 short-circuit, and
      `claimability.py`'s partial enumeration. Verified by reading each against the code it cites.
- [ ] AC5: behavior is unchanged for all seven current types. Verified by the existing gate and
      close-gate suites passing untouched, and by a test asserting the resolved exempt/reviewed
      sets equal the literals the six sites carried before this change.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "ticket_type or plan_review_exempt or partition" -q` — the
  partition, no-literals, and eighth-type tests (AC1, AC2, AC3).
- `python -m pytest tests/unit -q` — proves the six call sites still gate identically (AC5); these
  constants sit on the claim and close paths, so a mistake here is broad and loud.
- `make lint && make typecheck`.
